          available_excerpt: "27 \n \n(c) \nThe audited financial statements shall
            include or be accompanied by a \ncertificate of opinion of the independent
            certified public accountant or independent public \naccountant that is
            satisfactory in form and content to the [Commissioner]. If the certificate
            or \nopinion is qualified, the [Commissioner] may order the licensee to
            take any action as the \n[Commissioner] may find necessary to enable the
            independent or certified public accountant or \nindependent public accountant
            to remove the qualification. \nSection 7.03 Authorized Delegate Reporting.
            \n(a) \nEach licensee shall submit a report of authorized delegates within
            45 days \nof the end of the calendar quarter.20 The [Commissioner] is
            authorized and encouraged to utilize \nNMLS for the submission of the
            report required by this [Section 7.03(a)] provided that such \nfunctionality
            is consistent with the requirements of this [Section 7.03]. \n(b) \nThe
            authorized delegate report shall include, at a minimum, each authorized
            \ndelegate's: \n(1) \nCompany legal name; \n(2) \nTaxpayer employer identification
            number; \n(3) \nPrincipal provider identifier; \n(4) \nPhysical address;
            \n(5) \nMailing address; \n(6) \nAny business conducted in other states;
            \n(7) \nAny fictitious or trade name; \n(8) \nContact person name, phone
            number, and email \n(9) \nStart date as licensee’s authorized delegate;
            \n(10) \nEnd date acting as licensee’s authorized delegate, if applicable;
            \ \n(11) \n[Court orders pursuant to [Section 8.03];] and \n(12) \nAny
            other information the [Commissioner] reasonably requires with \nrespect
            to the authorized delegate. \nSection 7.04 Reports of Certain Events.21
            \n \n20 Commentary: This language is designed to implement state use of
            the NMLS Uniform Authorized Agent Reporting \n(UAAR) process. \n21 Commentary:
            States are encouraged to utilize NMLS to satisfy Section 7.04 reporting
            requirements if NMLS \ndevelops new functionality to prioritize reporting
            of significant events.\n"
        - source_id: SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538
          source_version: dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a
          title: '[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act'
          extraction_state: complete
          selected_passages:
          - unit_id: p000028
            start: 0
            end: 2132
            page_number: 28
            section_label: null
            body_hash: 80c098d06593529d6d6335e3b8a4fe8e8db356a8c5d82eb34a2001d27d642973
            path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000028.md
            text: "28 \n \n(a) \nA licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner]
              within one business \nday after the licensee has reason to know of the
              occurrence of any of the following events: \n(1) \nthe filing of a petition
              by or against the licensee under the \nUnited States Bankruptcy Code,
              11 U.S.C. Section 101-110, as amended or recodified from \ntime to time,
              for bankruptcy or reorganization; \n(2) \nthe filing of a petition by
              or against the licensee for \nreceivership, the commencement of any
              other judicial or administrative proceeding for its \ndissolution or
              reorganization, or the making of a general assignment for the benefit
              of its \ncreditors; or \n(3) \nthe commencement of a proceeding to revoke
              or suspend its \nlicense in a state or country in which the licensee
              engages in business or is licensed. \n(b) \nA licensee shall file a
              report with the [Commissioner] within three business \nday after the
              licensee has reason to know of the occurrence of any of the following
              events: \n(1) \na [charge or] conviction of the licensee or of a key
              individual \nor person in control of the licensee for a felony; or \n(2)
              \na [charge or] conviction of an authorized delegate for a \nfelony.
              \nSection 7.05 Bank Secrecy Act Reports. \nA licensee and an authorized
              delegate shall file all reports required by federal currency \nreporting,
              record keeping, and suspicious activity reporting requirements as set
              forth in the Bank \nSecrecy Act and other federal and state laws pertaining
              to money laundering. The timely filing of \na complete and accurate
              report required under this [Section 7.05] with the appropriate federal
              \nagency is deemed compliant with the requirements of this [Section
              7.05]. \nSection 7.06 Records. \n(a) \nLicensee shall maintain the following
              records, for determining its \ncompliance with this [Act] for at least
              [three] years: \n(1) \na record of each outstanding money transmission
              obligation \nsold; \n(2) \na general ledger posted at least monthly
              containing all asset, \nliability, capital, income, and expense accounts;
              \n(3) \nbank statements and bank reconciliation records; \n(4) \nrecords
              of outstanding money transmission obligations;\n"

            person in control of the licensee for a felony; or \n(2) \na [charge or]
            conviction of an authorized delegate for a \nfelony. \nSection 7.05 Bank
            Secrecy Act Reports. \nA licensee and an authorized delegate shall file
            all reports required by federal currency \nreporting, record keeping,
            and suspicious activity reporting requirements as set forth in the Bank
            \nSecrecy Act and other federal and state laws pertaining to money laundering.
            The timely filing of \na complete and accurate report required under this
            [Section 7.05] with the appropriate federal \nagency is deemed compliant
            with the requirements of this [Section 7.05]. \nSection 7.06 Records.
            \n(a) \nLicensee shall maintain the following records, for determining
            its \ncompliance with this [Act] for at least [three] years: \n(1) \na
            record of each outstanding money transmission obligation \nsold; \n(2)
            \na general ledger posted at least monthly containing all asset, \nliability,
            capital, income, and expense accounts; \n(3) \nbank statements and bank
            reconciliation records; \n(4) \nrecords of outstanding money transmission
            obligations;\n"

            text: "12 \n \n(4) \nThe terms of or a copy of any bond filed by a licensee,

              violation of this [Act] or regulations implementing this [Act]; and
              \n(e) \nImposition of an administrative fine or penalty under this [Act].
              \nSection 4.03 Supervision. \n(a) \nThe [Commissioner] may conduct an
              examination or investigation of a \nlicensee or authorized delegate
              or otherwise take independent action authorized by this [Act] or by
              \na rule adopted or order issued under this [Act] as reasonably necessary
              or appropriate to administer \nand enforce this [Act], regulations implementing
              this [Act], and other applicable law, including \nthe Bank Secrecy Act
              and the USA PATRIOT ACT.  The [Commissioner] may: \n(1) \nconduct an
              examination either on-site or off-site as the \n[Commissioner] may reasonably
              require; \n(2) \nconduct an examination in conjunction with an examination
              \nconducted by representatives of other state agencies or agencies of
              another state or of the \nfederal government; \n(3) \n  accept the examination
              report of another state agency or an agency \nof another state or of
              the federal government, or a report prepared by an independent \naccounting
              firm, which on being accepted is considered for all purposes as an official
              report \nof the [Commissioner]; and \n(4) \nsummon and examine under
              oath a key individual or employee of a \nlicensee or authorized delegate
              and require the person to produce records regarding any \nmatter related
              to the condition and business of the licensee or authorized delegate.
              \n(b) \nA licensee or authorized delegate shall provide, and the [Commissioner]
              \nshall have full and complete access to, all records the [Commissioner]
              may reasonably require to \nconduct a complete examination. The records
              must be provided at the location and in the format \nspecified by the
              [Commissioner], provided, the [Commissioner] may utilize multistate
              record \nproduction standards and examination procedures when such standards
              will reasonably achieve \nthe requirements of this [Section 4.03(b)].8
              \n(c) \nUnless otherwise directed by the [Commissioner], a licensee
              shall pay all \ncosts reasonably incurred in connection with an examination
              of the licensee or the licensee's \n \n8 Commentary: The [Commissioner]
              is encouraged to instruct examiners to: (1) include all examination
              requests in \nthe Day 1 letter that may require the licensee to obtain
              records located outside of the U.S., including but not limited \nto
              evidence demonstrating when an outstanding money transmission obligation
              has been extinguished; and (2) accept \nelectronic bank statements as
              provided to the licensee by the bank.\n"

            - issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-d22ea3957f21252a
              title: Open alerts, suspicious activity history, and acquisition diligence
              why_it_matters: About 40 open alerts and several suspicious activity
                reports remain unreviewed. Their contents could affect the acquisition
                decision, deal protections, remediation, and account migration.
              parent_issue_id: null
              fact_ids: []
              disposition: null
            questions:
            - question_id: Q-SAR
              text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                year been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
              consequence: Unread open alerts and SARs are the highest-risk item;
                they can create BSA/AML exposure that must be addressed before close
                and could affect the deal itself.
              state: answered
              answer: The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain
                in diligence.
              answer_kind: reported_fact
              linked_fact_ids:
              - FACT-20260909-070aec
            - question_id: Q-KYC
              text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
                and recordkeeping obligations?
              consequence: Whether the missing underlying documents create a compliance
                gap depends on how Mosaic plans to satisfy its own CIP/recordkeeping
                obligations for these users.
              state: answered
              answer: It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program permits
                reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance must confirm.
              answer_kind: reported_fact
              linked_fact_ids:
              - FACT-20260909-620c62
            - question_id: Q-MTL
              text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                before onboarding those customers?
              consequence: Whether the four new markets can be served at close depends
                on license transferability and state approval, which is a gating regulatory
                question.
              state: answered
              answer: Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor's licenses
                for the four new markets.
              answer_kind: reported_fact
              linked_fact_ids:
              - FACT-20260909-771ee1
            - question_id: Q-BONUS
              text: How is the $50 welcome bonus structured?
              consequence: The structure determines whether the bonus triggers consumer
                disclosure, funds-flow, or state promotional requirements.
              state: left_open
              answer: null
              answer_kind: null

              passages:
              - start: 0
                end: 3962
                text: '# Known Facts


                  - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
                  weeks out).

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                  - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by
                  Harbor.

                  - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
                  Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new
                  markets.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                  has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed
                  at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                  - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                  transfer, launching close+1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance.

                  - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
                  were already KYC''d.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                  results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to
                  Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                  - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                  (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)

                  - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                  on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or
                  is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                  - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                  the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                  Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or
                  apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                  - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                  what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer
                  identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known
                  whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s
                  prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

                  - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                  year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
                  and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                  what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                  before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                  to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                  ## Assumptions


                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                  and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
                  the acquisition without new state approval

                  - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                  Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                  documents

                  - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                  and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                  - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                  to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                  in 41 states (per the request).

                  - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                  purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert
                  obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                  '
              source_version: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409

                text: '# Harbor 2 — Harbor Pay acquisition migration (matter dossier)


                  Matter MAT-20260909-d89ad8 · prepared from captured records dated
                  Sep 9–10, 2026. Business question supplied by the matter record;
                  direction unchanged.


                  ## Current position


                  Yes — material parts of the Harbor Pay migration need legal review
                  before the Nov 15 close, and one item should be reviewed before
                  the deal terms are settled, not merely before launch. This is not
                  "just a data migration": the day-1 plan depends on results the records
                  show are unconfirmed — license coverage in the added markets, the
                  ability to rely on Harbor''s KYC without the underlying records,
                  and a monitoring cutover with no gap.


                  Three conditions decide how much of the full day-1 migration survives:


                  - **Whether Mosaic can lawfully serve each added market on day 1.**
                  The plan "use/assume Harbor''s licenses" is not established for
                  an asset purchase. If approvals are missing, those markets are a
                  post-close target, not day-1 access. (The number of added states
                  is itself unresolved — see Record conflicts.)


                  - **Whether Mosaic''s AML/CIP program and applicable rule permit
                  reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC**, and whether the pre-2023 cohort
                  with missing documents can keep full access without re-verification
                  or limits.


                  - **What the ~40 open alerts and the SAR history show**, and whether
                  monitoring transfers without a gap. The alert/SAR review is the
                  most decision-changing item because it can affect deal protections
                  and how affected customers are handled at migration.


                  The $50 bonus (launching close+1) and the customer-records/terms
                  side of the data move do not block close on today''s record, but
                  each must be reviewed before its own go-live point and each needs
                  documents not in the readable record.


                  What can proceed now: migration engineering, diligence, the compliance
                  data pull, the licensing map, and standing up a controlled review
                  protocol for the alerts/SARs. What should wait or change: launching
                  the added markets on Harbor''s licenses; full-access onboarding
                  of users whose verification cannot be evidenced; the monitoring
                  cutover unless a tested no-gap design or a bridge exists; the bonus
                  until its terms are reviewed.


                  This draft recommends treating those items as pre-close gates and
                  preparing a staged launch as the fallback. That is this draft''s
                  recommendation, not a recorded decision. The recorded plan is unchanged:
                  day-1 full migration, no re-verification, use/assume Harbor''s licenses,
                  bonus at close+1. The only recorded lawyer decisions are the Sep
                  9 intake answers (asset purchase; compliance to confirm KYC reliance;
                  alerts/SARs unreviewed; use/assume Harbor''s licenses). A complete
                  dossier rewrite was submitted as a tracked revision on Sep 10 and,
                  per the record, left the current dossier unchanged pending acceptance;
                  generating this draft records no new decision.


                  ## Decision question


                  Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal
                  review before the Nov 15 close?


                  ## Issues


                  The four workstreams below are the recorded issue set from the Sep
                  9 initial issue map ([source:MSG-20260909-efcbdd]) and the lawyer''s
                  "four issues" framing ([source:MSG-20260909-539d02]): licensing,
                  KYC/AML, alerts and monitoring, and marketing. The saved issue list
                  and its ISS identifiers were not inside this run''s readable material,
                  so no issue IDs or markers are asserted here. A fifth issue, newly
                  identified in this draft from the recorded migration plan, is included
                  and labeled.


                  Support status: no retrieved external authority appears in the readable
                  records. The record shows the lawyer asked for research with sources
                  ([source:MSG-20260909-660683], [source:MSG-20260909-406e0e]), an
                  initial "research is in progress" statement ([source:MSG-20260909-168b9d])
                  later corrected ([source:MSG-20260909-91b5ec], [source:MSG-20260909-b4cc1f]),
                  and a run described as "queued or running" with saved source choices
                  ([source:MSG-20260910-c27e90]); no run output was readable here.
                  Every legal proposition below is therefore a framework or lead,
                  not verified support; named authorities carry **Needs checking**.
                  Each issue gets an initial answer; any prior researched issue answers
                  in the nine captured documents were not readable in this run and
                  should be merged when available.


                  ### 1. State money transmitter licensing for the added markets


                  **Current answer**


                  Not established for day 1. An asset purchase does not automatically
                  carry Harbor''s money transmitter licenses to Mosaic, and a separate
                  legal entity cannot simply "use" another company''s licenses. Until
                  a state-by-state path exists — new license, transfer or change-of-control
                  approval in the transaction, or an arrangement where the licensed
                  entity performs the transmission — the added markets should be treated
                  as post-close, not part of day-1 full access. Even where Mosaic
                  holds its own license, the account migration may trigger state notices
                  or filings (unverified).


                  **Rule and support**


                  State money transmitter statutes generally require a license, or
                  status as an authorized delegate of a licensee, to transmit money
                  for others; licenses are issued to a specific entity, and state
                  approval is commonly required for a change of control or transfer
                  of a licensed business [**Needs checking** — the MTL statutes of
                  the specific states; the CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act
                  where adopted]. Federal MSB registration (31 C.F.R. § 1022.380)
                  is a separate requirement and does not substitute for state licensure
                  [**Needs checking**]. The precise research question: for each state
                  where Mosaic lacks a license and Harbor holds one, what route lets
                  Mosaic lawfully serve migrated customers — new license, license
                  transfer, change-of-control approval, or authorized-delegate arrangement
                  — on what timeline, and what customer or regulator notices accompany
                  the change?


                  **Application**


                  Recorded: asset purchase (intake answer, [source:MSG-20260909-2e549e]);
                  Mosaic 41 licenses; Harbor 38; combined 44; plan "use/assume Harbor''s
                  licenses"; full acce'

              passages:
              - start: 0
                end: 5937
                text: '## Harbor 2 — preparation note (close targeted Nov 15)


                  **Controlling question:** does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition
                  migration need legal review before the Nov 15 close? The newest
                  turn ("Generate the Dossier") and the surrounding bank-held-funds
                  comparisons are supporting work; they do not change that question.
                  The record contains **no recorded decisions** at all, all five registered
                  issues are `open`, and one intake question — how the $50 bonus is
                  structured — was left open with no answer.


                  **Lawyer reframe.** Dana''s framing is "it''s really just a data
                  migration." The reframe is that the migration *is* the regulated
                  event: on day 1 Mosaic Relay onboards 252,000 accounts into its
                  own licensed product set with no re-verification, repoints monitoring,
                  and launches a cash offer — under an asset-purchase structure in
                  which nothing about Harbor''s licenses or compliance record transfers
                  by default. The operative question is therefore not "can we inherit
                  Harbor''s status," but **"what must Mosaic obtain, file, decide
                  or preserve in its own name before Nov 15, and which parts of the
                  stated deal upside are not actually available at close."**


                  **Three premises the record lets us test**


                  1. *"Just a data migration."* Fails. The day-1 cutover is the moment
                  CIP, licensing, monitoring and disclosure obligations attach to
                  252k accounts.

                  2. *"44 states is a nice win — opens four new markets."* Fails on
                  the arithmetic and on the law. Harbor 38 + Mosaic 41 with a 44-state
                  union yields **three** new states, not four, and the states are
                  never named; and the plan to "use/assume" Harbor''s licenses rests
                  on an assumption the record still marks open ([source:ASM-20260909-29b823]),
                  against the saved position that transferability should not be relied
                  on without a state rule, approval or written regulator position.

                  3. *"No re-verification — they were already KYC''d."* Unresolved.
                  Whether Mosaic''s own AML/CIP program permits reliance is unknown,
                  and the pre-2023 records cannot be recovered (vendor shut down in
                  2024; only pass/fail survives).


                  **Different route the evidence supports.** Run the remaining ~9
                  weeks as a *gated launch*, not a documentation exercise: read and
                  preserve the alert/SAR backlog; decide KYC reliance per cohort and
                  schedule remediation; prove or drop the Harbor-only states; validate
                  the monitoring cutover with a parallel run; paper notice/consent,
                  new customer terms and closing conditions. If a gate fails, migrate
                  only in the overlapping states on day 1 and onboard KYC-deficient
                  accounts with limits — a scoped migration rather than the full one.


                  **Material issues.** Five registered: money transmission licensing
                  (44-state footprint); BSA/AML and KYC reliance for pre-2023 users;
                  SAR and alert handling (~40 open alerts, unreviewed); monitoring
                  vendor transition at close; $50 welcome bonus. Three that are missing
                  and material: **migration data handling and customer notice** (the
                  piece the request actually calls "just a data migration," never
                  analyzed); **pre-close papering** (closing conditions, interim operation,
                  allocation of the alert/SAR and KYC-record risk — no draft or terms
                  appear anywhere); and **post-close access to Harbor''s alert/case
                  history** (the records live in the SaaS system whose contract ends
                  at close).


                  **Three business priorities** — ranked by effect on the business
                  question, time-fixedness and irreversibility, not by difficulty:


                  1. **Read and preserve the alert/SAR backlog before anything else
                  is scheduled.** It is the only item that can change the deal itself;
                  it is entirely unread, so no one can yet say whether a filing is
                  late or an account must be excluded; and the records needed to answer
                  it may become inaccessible at close.

                  2. **Decide KYC reliance for the pre-2023 cohort — rely, re-verify,
                  or restrict access.** It determines whether "no re-verification"
                  is available at all for the largest population; the underlying documents
                  cannot be recreated; and re-verifying or limiting a cohort is a
                  multi-week program that has to be decided before close, not after.

                  3. **Prove the Harbor-only states can be served at close, or pull
                  them from day-1 scope.** It tests the premise the deal is being
                  sold on, state timelines are the longest external dependency and
                  cannot be compressed, and serving a state without authority is a
                  violation later paperwork cannot undo.


                  **Research these first:** the SAR/alert backlog ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38]),
                  KYC reliance ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045]), and the
                  licensing position for the Harbor-only states ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045])
                  — in that order. If the team needs the earliest single go/no-go
                  decision, licensing converts fastest — but it should still follow
                  the backlog read, because a live SAR problem can outrank market
                  access.


                  **Watch-outs.** The bank-held-funds structure is a saved hypothetical
                  and was never adopted; later turns ran under that scenario path,
                  and some prior dossier drafts carry scenario scope, so their conclusions
                  are not findings about this acquisition. The licensing research
                  has **no citable support** (4 sources retrieved, 0 passages read;
                  one output headed "No external authority retrieved"), and repeated
                  "research queued/running" messages are status, not results. Assumption
                  [source:ASM-20260909-57e86b] still calls the structure unconfirmed
                  although the asset purchase is recorded and was reconfirmed twice
                  by the user. The matter''s `target_date` field (2026-09-11) sits
                  oddly against activity through 2026-09-12 — treat it as unverified.
                  Urgent below marks the five items where the close date itself fixes
                  the deadline and a mistake cannot be cured afterwards; it is not
                  the same as the top-three ranking.


                  *Not performed: no web research. Full-text reads covered the request,
                  facts register, intake answers and early analysis; the licensing
                  packet was reviewed at excerpt level and prior dossiers treated
                  as fallible synthesis.*

                  '
              source_version: 8da355f4654a8c9ef63ed45c11e80f7b1870be7b0eee84f77e33b55939d63b73

          available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


            - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks
            out).

            - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
            Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance
            and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

            - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by Harbor.

            - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
            Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.

            - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has
            pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users
            onboarded before 2023.

            - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
            terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at
            Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

            - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
            launching close+1.

            - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
            last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

            - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
            Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.

            - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were
            already KYC''d.

            - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
            results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users
            onboarded before 2023.

            - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
            terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
            Relay''s engine on day 1.

            - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
            last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

            - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
            buys Harbor''s assets)

            - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another
            institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
            required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

            - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
            last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

            - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic
            Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its
            own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

            - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what
            is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
            and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s
            AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must
            confirm.

            - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
            been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history
            have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

            - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
            is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before
            onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume
            Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


            ## Assumptions


            - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and
            Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition
            without new state approval

            - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
            Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents

            - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
            validated before close without a monitoring gap

            - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state
            MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

            - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
            41 states (per the request).

            - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
            which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
            (structure not yet confirmed).

            '

          available_excerpt: '# Harbor 2 — Harbor Pay acquisition migration (matter
            dossier)


            Matter MAT-20260909-d89ad8 · prepared from captured records dated Sep
            9–10, 2026. Business question supplied by the matter record; direction
            unchanged.


            ## Current position


            Yes — material parts of the Harbor Pay migration need legal review before
            the Nov 15 close, and one item should be reviewed before the deal terms
            are settled, not merely before launch. This is not "just a data migration":
            the day-1 plan depends on results the records show are unconfirmed — license
            coverage in the added markets, the ability to rely on Harbor''s KYC without
            the underlying records, and a monitoring cutover with no gap.


            Three conditions decide how much of the full day-1 migration survives:


            - **Whether Mosaic can lawfully serve each added market on day 1.** The
            plan "use/assume Harbor''s licenses" is not established for an asset purchase.
            If approvals are missing, those markets are a post-close target, not day-1
            access. (The number of added states is itself unresolved — see Record
            conflicts.)


            - **Whether Mosaic''s AML/CIP program and applicable rule permit reliance
            on Harbor''s prior KYC**, and whether the pre-2023 cohort with missing
            documents can keep full access without re-verification or limits.


            - **What the ~40 open alerts and the SAR history show**, and whether monitoring
            transfers without a gap. The alert/SAR review is the most decision-changing
            item because it can affect deal protections and how affected customers
            are handled at migration.


            The $50 bonus (launching close+1) and the customer-records/terms side
            of the data move do not block close on today''s record, but each must
            be reviewed before its own go-live point and each needs documents not
            in the readable record.


            What can proceed now: migration engineering, diligence, the compliance
            data pull, the licensing map, and standing up a controlled review protocol
            for the alerts/SARs. What should wait or change: launching the added markets
            on Harbor''s licenses; full-access onboarding of users whose verification
            cannot be evidenced; the monitoring cutover unless a tested no-gap design
            or a bridge exists; the bonus until its terms are reviewed.


            This draft recommends treating those items as pre-close gates and preparing
            a staged launch as the fallback. That is this draft''s recommendation,
            not a recorded decision. The recorded plan is unchanged: day-1 full migration,
            no re-verification, use/assume Harbor''s licenses, bonus at close+1. The
            only recorded lawyer decisions are the Sep 9 intake answers (asset purchase;
            compliance to confirm KYC reliance; alerts/SARs unreviewed; use/assume
            Harbor''s licenses). A complete dossier rewrite was submitted as a tracked
            revision on Sep 10 and, per the record, left the current dossier unchanged
            pending acceptance; generating this draft records no new decision.


            ## Decision question


            Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal review
            before the Nov 15 close?


            ## Issues


            The four workstreams below are the recorded issue set from the Sep 9 initial
            issue map ([source:MSG-20260909-efcbdd]) and the lawyer''s "four issues"
            framing ([source:MSG-20260909-539d02]): licensing, KYC/AML, alerts and
            monitoring, and marketing. The saved issue list and its ISS identifiers
            were not inside this run''s readable material, so no issue IDs or markers
            are asserted here. A fifth issue, newly identified in this draft from
            the recorded migration plan, is included and labeled.


            Support status: no retrieved external authority appears in the readable
            records. The record shows the lawyer asked for research with sources ([source:MSG-20260909-660683],
            [source:MSG-20260909-406e0e]), an initial "research is in progress" statement
            ([source:MSG-20260909-168b9d]) later corrected ([source:MSG-20260909-91b5ec],
            [source:MSG-20260909-b4cc1f]), and a run described as "queued or running"
            with saved source choices ([source:MSG-20260910-c27e90]); no run output
            was readable here. Every legal proposition below is therefore a framework
            or lead, not verified support; named authorities carry **Needs checking**.
            Each issue gets an initial answer; any prior researched issue answers
            in the nine captured documents were not readable in this run and should
            be merged when available.


            ### 1. State money transmitter licensing for the added markets


            **Current answer**


            Not established for day 1. An asset purchase does not automatically carry
            Harbor''s money transmitter licenses to Mosaic, and a separate legal entity
            cannot simply "use" another company''s licenses. Until a state-by-state
            path exists — new license, transfer or change-of-control approval in the
            transaction, or an arrangement where the licensed entity performs the
            transmission — the added markets should be treated as post-close, not
            part of day-1 full access. Even where Mosaic holds its own license, the
            account migration may trigger state notices or filings (unverified).


            **Rule and support**


            State money transmitter statutes generally require a license, or status
            as an authorized delegate of a licensee, to transmit money for others;
            licenses are issued to a specific entity, and state approval is commonly
            required for a change of control or transfer of a licensed business [**Needs
            checking** — the MTL statutes of the specific states; the CSBS Money Transmission
            Modernization Act where adopted]. Federal MSB registration (31 C.F.R.
            § 1022.380) is a separate requirement and does not substitute for state
            licensure [**Needs checking**]. The precise research question: for each
            state where Mosaic lacks a license and Harbor holds one, what route lets
            Mosaic lawfully serve migrated customers — new license, license transfer,
            change-of-control approval, or authorized-delegate arrangement — on what
            timeline, and what customer or regulator notices accompany the change?


            **Application**


            Recorded: asset purchase (intake answer, [source:MSG-20260909-2e549e]);
            Mosaic 41 licenses; Harbor 38; combined 44; plan "use/assume Harbor''s
            licenses"; full acce'

            the Dossier") and the surrounding bank-held-funds comparisons are supporting
            work; they do not change that question. The record contains **no recorded
            decisions** at all, all five registered issues are `open`, and one intake
            question — how the $50 bonus is structured — was left open with no answer.


            **Lawyer reframe.** Dana''s framing is "it''s really just a data migration."
            The reframe is that the migration *is* the regulated event: on day 1 Mosaic
            Relay onboards 252,000 accounts into its own licensed product set with
            no re-verification, repoints monitoring, and launches a cash offer — under
            an asset-purchase structure in which nothing about Harbor''s licenses
            or compliance record transfers by default. The operative question is therefore
            not "can we inherit Harbor''s status," but **"what must Mosaic obtain,
            file, decide or preserve in its own name before Nov 15, and which parts
            of the stated deal upside are not actually available at close."**


            **Three premises the record lets us test**


            1. *"Just a data migration."* Fails. The day-1 cutover is the moment CIP,
            licensing, monitoring and disclosure obligations attach to 252k accounts.

            2. *"44 states is a nice win — opens four new markets."* Fails on the
            arithmetic and on the law. Harbor 38 + Mosaic 41 with a 44-state union
            yields **three** new states, not four, and the states are never named;
            and the plan to "use/assume" Harbor''s licenses rests on an assumption
            the record still marks open ([source:ASM-20260909-29b823]), against the
            saved position that transferability should not be relied on without a
            state rule, approval or written regulator position.

            3. *"No re-verification — they were already KYC''d."* Unresolved. Whether
            Mosaic''s own AML/CIP program permits reliance is unknown, and the pre-2023
            records cannot be recovered (vendor shut down in 2024; only pass/fail
            survives).


            **Different route the evidence supports.** Run the remaining ~9 weeks
            as a *gated launch*, not a documentation exercise: read and preserve the
            alert/SAR backlog; decide KYC reliance per cohort and schedule remediation;
            prove or drop the Harbor-only states; validate the monitoring cutover
            with a parallel run; paper notice/consent, new customer terms and closing
            conditions. If a gate fails, migrate only in the overlapping states on
            day 1 and onboard KYC-deficient accounts with limits — a scoped migration
            rather than the full one.


            **Material issues.** Five registered: money transmission licensing (44-state
            footprint); BSA/AML and KYC reliance for pre-2023 users; SAR and alert
            handling (~40 open alerts, unreviewed); monitoring vendor transition at
            close; $50 welcome bonus. Three that are missing and material: **migration
            data handling and customer notice** (the piece the request actually calls
            "just a data migration," never analyzed); **pre-close papering** (closing
            conditions, interim operation, allocation of the alert/SAR and KYC-record
            risk — no draft or terms appear anywhere); and **post-close access to
            Harbor''s alert/case history** (the records live in the SaaS system whose
            contract ends at close).


            **Three business priorities** — ranked by effect on the business question,
            time-fixedness and irreversibility, not by difficulty:


            1. **Read and preserve the alert/SAR backlog before anything else is scheduled.**
            It is the only item that can change the deal itself; it is entirely unread,
            so no one can yet say whether a filing is late or an account must be excluded;
            and the records needed to answer it may become inaccessible at close.

            2. **Decide KYC reliance for the pre-2023 cohort — rely, re-verify, or
            restrict access.** It determines whether "no re-verification" is available
            at all for the largest population; the underlying documents cannot be
            recreated; and re-verifying or limiting a cohort is a multi-week program
            that has to be decided before close, not after.

            3. **Prove the Harbor-only states can be served at close, or pull them
            from day-1 scope.** It tests the premise the deal is being sold on, state
            timelines are the longest external dependency and cannot be compressed,
            and serving a state without authority is a violation later paperwork cannot
            undo.


            **Research these first:** the SAR/alert backlog ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38]),
            KYC reliance ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045]), and the licensing
            position for the Harbor-only states ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045])
            — in that order. If the team needs the earliest single go/no-go decision,
            licensing converts fastest — but it should still follow the backlog read,
            because a live SAR problem can outrank market access.


            **Watch-outs.** The bank-held-funds structure is a saved hypothetical
            and was never adopted; later turns ran under that scenario path, and some
            prior dossier drafts carry scenario scope, so their conclusions are not
            findings about this acquisition. The licensing research has **no citable
            support** (4 sources retrieved, 0 passages read; one output headed "No
            external authority retrieved"), and repeated "research queued/running"
            messages are status, not results. Assumption [source:ASM-20260909-57e86b]
            still calls the structure unconfirmed although the asset purchase is recorded
            and was reconfirmed twice by the user. The matter''s `target_date` field
            (2026-09-11) sits oddly against activity through 2026-09-12 — treat it
            as unverified. Urgent below marks the five items where the close date
            itself fixes the deadline and a mistake cannot be cured afterwards; it
            is not the same as the top-three ranking.


            *Not performed: no web research. Full-text reads covered the request,
            facts register, intake answers and early analysis; the licensing packet
            was reviewed at excerpt level and prior dossiers treated as fallible synthesis.*

            '

        message_id: MSG-20260913-b9ca89
      priorities:
      - key: protect_acquisition
        text: Determine whether unresolved compliance matters change the acquisition
          decision or deal protections.
        why: The findings could affect valuation, liability, closing conditions, remediation,
          or whether Mosaic should close.
        issue_ids:
        - ISS-c9d7c39f63-9699bb16b60412ba
        - ISS-c9d7c39f63-4c1eee0ce2e8b327
        changed: false
      - key: confirm_launch_authority
        text: Confirm where and how Mosaic can lawfully operate on day one.
        why: License approvals can take time. Harbor's licenses cannot safely be treated
          as transferable without review.
        issue_ids:
        - ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045
        changed: false
      - key: prevent_compliance_gap
        text: Establish adequate identity records and uninterrupted monitoring before
          migration.
        why: The plan affects about 252,000 accounts and could create a large problem
          that is difficult to reverse.
        issue_ids:
        - ISS-c9d7c39f63-a6daa6bde380da74
        - ISS-c9d7c39f63-034e6643b5481b97
        - ISS-c9d7c39f63-782d624fe465f404
        changed: false

      new_issue_candidates:
      - candidate_key: alerts_sars_deal_risk
        title: Unresolved alerts, suspicious activity reports, and acquisition risk
        why_it_matters: About 40 alerts and several suspicious activity reports remain
          unreviewed. Their contents could affect liability, remediation, transaction
          protections, or the closing decision.
        initial_answer: Review is required before closing. The final assessment depends
          on the contents and status of the alerts and reports, related account activity,
          Harbor's response, and the acquisition agreement's disclosure and liability
          terms.
        next_action: Have authorized compliance personnel review the alert and report
          history. Give deal counsel an appropriate findings summary and compare it
          with the acquisition representations, disclosures, indemnities, closing
          conditions, and remediation duties.
        focused_topic: anti-money-laundering diligence and unresolved alerts in a
          payment company acquisition
        fact_ids: []
        parent_issue_id: null
        urgent: true
      - candidate_key: kyc_records_reverification
        title: Reliance on Harbor identity checks and missing records
        why_it_matters: Mosaic plans to move about 252,000 accounts without new verification.
          The former identity vendor closed, and the underlying records are unavailable.
        initial_answer: Pass-or-fail results might not satisfy Mosaic's program or
          applicable account requirements. The answer depends on Mosaic's written
          customer identification and anti-money-laundering program, the Harbor records
          still available, customer risk levels, and the legal basis for reliance.
        next_action: Compare Harbor's available records with Mosaic's required customer
          files. Select documented reliance, risk-based re-verification, account limits,
          or delayed migration for each affected group.
        focused_topic: customer identification reliance and missing verification records
          after a payment company acquisition
        fact_ids: []
        parent_issue_id: null
        urgent: true
      - candidate_key: monitoring_continuity
        title: Transaction-monitoring continuity at closing
        why_it_matters: Harbor's monitoring service ends at closing while its feed
          moves to Mosaic. A failed change could create an immediate monitoring gap.
        initial_answer: The record does not show that the new monitoring arrangement
          has been validated. Adequacy depends on field mapping, rule coverage, historical-data
          access, testing, alert ownership, cutover timing, and fallback service.
        next_action: Complete documented testing and reconciliation before ending
          the old service. Assign ownership of alerts across the cutover and retain
          a fallback or delay the migration if testing fails.
        focused_topic: transaction monitoring continuity during a payment platform
          acquisition
        fact_ids: []
        parent_issue_id: alerts_sars_deal_risk
        urgent: true
      - candidate_key: customer_account_data_transfer
        title: Customer accounts, contracts, balances, data, and product access
        why_it_matters: The migration changes where customers receive service and
          gives them unified balances and access to Mosaic products. This can affect
          contracts, notices, privacy, eligibility, and customer rights.
        initial_answer: The record does not establish that every account, contract,
          balance, and data set can move automatically. The answer depends on assignment
          terms, notices or consents, data types and destinations, product eligibility,
          balance treatment, safeguards, and rollback ability.
        next_action: Map each proposed transfer. Identify required notices, consents,
          disclosures, checks, safeguards, and rollback steps. Hold irreversible transfers
          until review is complete.
        focused_topic: customer and data migration in a payment business asset acquisition
        fact_ids:
        - FACT-20260909-551367
        parent_issue_id: null
        urgent: true
      - candidate_key: transaction_documents_migration
        title: Acquisition terms, risk allocation, and migration authority
        why_it_matters: The transaction documents must cover the purchased assets,
          assumed liabilities, regulatory dependencies, records delivery, consents,
          and post-close cooperation.
        initial_answer: The record confirms an asset purchase but does not establish
          that the transaction documents support every migration step. The answer
          depends on the signed agreement, schedules, assumed contracts and liabilities,
          covenants, consents, and closing conditions.
        next_action: Map the migration plan and diligence findings to the transaction
          documents. Add or enforce protections for alerts, records, licenses, monitoring,
          remediation, and cooperation as needed.
        focused_topic: compliance risk allocation and migration conditions in a payment
          business asset purchase
        fact_ids:
        - FACT-20260909-ed9f06
        parent_issue_id: null
        urgent: true
      - candidate_key: welcome_bonus
        title: Fifty-dollar welcome bonus
        why_it_matters: The offer can create advertising, eligibility, disclosure,
          payment, expiration, tax, and complaint risks.
        initial_answer: Review is required before launch, but the visible record does
          not show that this issue affects closing. The answer depends on the final
          terms, eligible customers, required actions, payment method, restrictions,
          marketing text, and launch markets.
        next_action: Draft complete offer terms and review all customer messages.
          Delay the promotion if higher-priority migration controls are incomplete.
        focused_topic: payment account welcome bonus terms and consumer protection
        fact_ids: []
        parent_issue_id: customer_account_data_transfer
        urgent: false

      preparation: '## Preparation note


        **Result:** Yes. Legal and compliance review is needed before the Nov 15 close.


        **Lawyer reframe:** Identify which migration risks can change the acquisition
        decision, need approval before launch, or cause harm that Mosaic cannot easily
        reverse.


        This is not only a data migration. The plan moves 240,000 consumers and 12,000
        businesses on day one after closing. Mosaic also plans to rely on Harbor’s
        prior identity checks and licenses.


        ### Material issues


        - About 40 alerts and several suspicious activity reports have not been reviewed.

        - The deal is an asset purchase. The record does not prove that Harbor’s money-transmitter
        licenses will transfer or support Mosaic.

        - Harbor’s former identity vendor closed in 2024. Mosaic has results but lacks
        underlying identity records.

        - Harbor’s monitoring service ends at closing. Mosaic must prevent a monitoring
        gap.

        - Account, balance, contract, data, and product-access changes can require
        notices, consent, or new checks.

        - The acquisition documents must allocate these risks and support the migration.

        - The $50 welcome bonus needs review before launch, but it is not a first
        closing priority.


        ### Three business priorities


        1. **Protect the acquisition decision.** Review the alerts and suspicious
        activity history. The results could affect closing terms, liability, price,
        or the decision to close.

        2. **Confirm lawful day-one operations.** Do not assume Harbor’s licenses
        can support Mosaic in four new markets.

        3. **Prevent a large compliance gap.** Confirm identity records and monitoring
        continuity before moving 252,000 accounts.


        ### First three issues to research


        1. Unresolved alerts, suspicious activity reports, and their effect on the
        deal.

        2. License transfer and approval requirements for the four new markets.

        3. Whether Mosaic can rely on Harbor’s identity checks without the underlying
        records.


        The saved-record limit prevented recovery of most existing issue IDs. The
        plan uses the one available exact ID and candidate keys for issues whose IDs
        could not be verified.




        > A requested saved-record read was unavailable. The writer used the material
        available.

        '

    title: request.md
    support_state: supplied
    source_type: workspace
    available_excerpt: '# Original Request


      From: Dana, PM — Growth & Integration

      Subject: Harbor migration — anything here need legal?


      We''re acquiring Harbor Pay. Close is targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks). Migration
      plan:


      240k consumer users, 12k business accounts move into our app on day 1 post-close.
      One unified account, one balance, full access to our product set.

      No re-verification — they were already KYC''d by Harbor.

      Harbor holds MTLs in 38 states, we hold 41. Combined that''s 44 — nice win,
      opens four new markets.

      Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024. We have pass/fail
      results for everyone, but not the underlying documents for users onboarded before
      2023.

      Harbor''s monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close.
      Plan is to repoint their transaction feed at our engine on day 1.

      Marketing wants a "Welcome" campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer, launching
      close+1.

      Diligence flagged that Harbor has ~40 open alerts and "a handful" of SARs from
      the last year. Nobody''s read them yet.


      Does any of this need legal before close? It''s really just a data migration.

      '

        Title 31—Money and Finance: Treasury


        Subtitle B—Regulations Relating to Money and Finance


        CHAPTER X—FINANCIAL CRIMES ENFORCEMENT NETWORK, DEPARTMENT OF THE TREASURY


        PART 1022—RULES FOR MONEY SERVICES BUSINESSES


        Subpart B—Programs


        § 1022.210 Anti-money laundering programs for money services businesses.


        31 CFR § 1022.210 - Anti-money laundering programs for money services businesses.


        CFR


        prev | next


        § 1022.210 Anti-money laundering programs for money services businesses.


        (a) Each money services business, as defined by § 1010.100(ff) of this chapter,
        shall develop, implement, and maintain an effective anti-money laundering
        program. An effective anti-money laundering program is one that is reasonably
        designed to prevent the money services business from being used to facilitate
        money laundering and the financing of terrorist activities.


        (b) The program shall be commensurate with the risks posed by the location
        and size of, and the nature and volume of the financial services provided
        by, the money services business.


        (c) The program shall be in writing, and a money services business shall make
        copies of the anti-money laundering program available for inspection to the
        Department of the Treasury upon request.


        (d) At a minimum, the program shall:


        (1) Incorporate policies, procedures, and internal controls reasonably designed
        to assure compliance with this chapter.


        (i) Policies, procedures, and internal controls developed and implemented
        under this section shall include provisions for complying with the requirements
        of this chapter including, to the extent applicable to the money services
        business, requirements for:


        (A) Verifying customer identification, including as set forth in paragraph
        (d)(1)(iv) of this section;


        (B) Filing Reports;


        (C) Creating and retaining records;


        (D) Responding to law enforcement requests.


        (ii) Money services businesses that have automated data processing systems
        should integrate their compliance procedures with such systems.


        (iii) A person that is a money services business solely because it is an agent
        for another money services business as set forth in § 1022.380(a)(3) , and
        the money services business for which it serves as agent, may by agreement
        allocate between them responsibility for development of policies, procedures,
        and internal controls required by this paragraph (d)(1). Each money services
        business shall remain solely responsible for implementation of the requirements
        set forth in this section, and nothing in this paragraph (d)(1) relieves any
        money services business from its obligation to establish and maintain an effective
        anti-money laundering program.


        (iv) A money services business that is a provider or seller of prepaid access
        must establish procedures to verify the identity of a person who obtains prepaid
        access under a prepaid program and obtain identifying information concerning
        such a person , including name, date of birth, address, and identification
        number. Sellers of prepaid access must also establish procedures to verify
        the identity of a person who obtains prepaid access to funds that exceed $10,000
        during any one day and obtain identifying information concerning such a person
        , including name, date of birth, address, and identification number. Providers
        of prepaid access must retain access to such identifying information for five
        years after the last use of the prepaid access device or vehicle; such information
        obtained by sellers of prepaid access must be retained for five years from
        the date of the sale of the prepaid access device or vehicle.


        (2) Designate a person to assure day to day compliance with the program and
        this chapter. The responsibilities of such person shall include assuring that:


        (i) The money services business properly files reports, and creates and retains
        records, in accordance with applicable requirements of this chapter;


        (ii) The compliance program is updated as necessary to reflect current requirements
        of this chapter, and related guidance issued by the Department of the Treasury
        ; and


        (iii) The money services business provides appropriate training and education
        in accordance with paragraph (d)(3) of this section.


        (3) Provide education and/or training of appropriate personnel concerning
        their responsibilities under the program, including training in the detection
        of suspicious transactions to the extent that the money services business
        is required to report such transactions under this chapter.


        (4) Provide for independent review to monitor and maintain an adequate program.
        The scope and frequency of the review shall be commensurate with the risk
        of the financial services provided by the money services business. Such review
        may be conducted by an officer or employee of the money services business
        so long as the reviewer is not the person designated in paragraph (d)(2) of
        this section.'

      (2) Designate a person to assure day to day compliance with the program and

        Title 31—Money and Finance: Treasury


        Subtitle B—Regulations Relating to Money and Finance


        CHAPTER X—FINANCIAL CRIMES ENFORCEMENT NETWORK, DEPARTMENT OF THE TREASURY


        PART 1022—RULES FOR MONEY SERVICES BUSINESSES


        Subpart C—Reports Required To Be Made By Money Services Businesses


        § 1022.320 Reports by money services businesses of suspicious transactions.


        31 CFR § 1022.320 - Reports by money services businesses of suspicious transactions.


        CFR


        Table of Popular Names


        prev | next


        § 1022.320 Reports by money services businesses of suspicious transactions.


        (a)  General.


        (1) Every money services business described in § 1010.100(ff)(1) , (3), (4),
        (5), (6), and (7) of this chapter, shall file with the Treasury Department,
        to the extent and in the manner required by this section, a report of any
        suspicious transaction relevant to a possible violation of law or regulation.
        Any money services business may also file with the Treasury Department, by
        using the form specified in paragraph (b)(1) of this section, or otherwise,
        a report of any suspicious transaction that it believes is relevant to the
        possible violation of any law or regulation but whose reporting is not required
        by this section.


        (2) A transaction requires reporting under the terms of this section if it
        is conducted or attempted by, at, or through a money services business, involves
        or aggregates funds or other assets of at least $2,000 (except as provided
        in paragraph (a)(3) of this section), and the money services business knows,
        suspects, or has reason to suspect that the transaction (or a pattern of transactions
        of which the transaction is a part):


        (i) Involves funds derived from illegal activity or is intended or conducted
        in order to hide or disguise funds or assets derived from illegal activity
        (including, without limitation, the ownership, nature, source, location, or
        control of such funds or assets) as part of a plan to violate or evade any
        Federal law or regulation or to avoid any transaction reporting requirement
        under Federal law or regulation;


        (ii) Is designed, whether through structuring or other means, to evade any
        requirements of this chapter or of any other regulations promulgated under
        the Bank Secrecy Act ; or


        (iii) Serves no business or apparent lawful purpose, and the reporting money
        services business knows of no reasonable explanation for the transaction after
        examining the available facts, including the background and possible purpose
        of the transaction .


        (iv) Involves use of the money services business to facilitate criminal activity.


        (3) To the extent that the identification of transactions required to be reported
        is derived from a review of clearance records or other similar records of
        money orders or traveler''s checks that have been sold or processed, an issuer
        of money orders or traveler''s checks shall only be required to report a transaction
        or pattern of transactions that involves or aggregates funds or other assets
        of at least $5,000.


        (4) The obligation to identify and properly and timely to report a suspicious
        transaction rests with each money services business involved in the transaction
        , provided that no more than one report is required to be filed by the money
        services businesses involved in a particular transaction (so long as the report
        filed contains all relevant facts). Whether, in addition to any liability
        on its own for failure to report, a money services business that issues the
        instrument or provides the funds transfer service involved in the transaction
        may be liable for the failure of another money services business involved
        in the transaction to report that transaction depends upon the nature of the
        contractual or other relationship between the businesses, and the legal effect
        of the facts and circumstances of the relationship and transaction involved,
        under general principles of the law of agency.


        (b)  Filing procedures —(1) What to file. A suspicious transaction shall be
        reported by completing a Suspicious Activity Report(“SAR”), and collecting
        and maintaining supporting documentation as required by paragraph (c) of this
        section.


        (2)  Where to file. The SAR shall be filed in a central location to be determined
        by FinCEN , as indicated in the instructions to the SAR.'

        Title 31—Money and Finance: Treasury


        Subtitle B—Regulations Relating to Money and Finance


        CHAPTER X—FINANCIAL CRIMES ENFORCEMENT NETWORK, DEPARTMENT OF THE TREASURY


        PART 1010—GENERAL PROVISIONS


        Subpart D—Records Required To Be Maintained


        § 1010.430 Nature of records and retention period.


        31 CFR § 1010.430 - Nature of records and retention period.


        CFR


        prev | next


        § 1010.430 Nature of records and retention period.


        (a) Wherever it is required that there be retained either the original or
        a copy or reproduction of a check, draft, monetary instrument , investment
        security , or other similar instrument, there shall be retained a copy of
        both front and back of each such instrument or document, except that no copy
        need be retained of the back of any instrument or document which is entirely
        blank or which contains only standardized printed information, a copy of which
        is on file.


        (b) Records required by this chapter to be retained by financial institutions
        may be those made in the ordinary course of business by a financial institution
        . If no record is made in the ordinary course of business of any transaction
        with respect to which records are required to be retained by this chapter,
        then such a record shall be prepared in writing by the financial institution
        .


        (c) The rules and regulations issued by the Internal Revenue Service under
        26 U.S.C. 6109 determine what constitutes a taxpayer identification number
        and whose number shall be obtained in the case of an account maintained by
        one or more persons.


        (d) All records that are required to be retained by this chapter shall be
        retained for a period of five years. Records or reports required to be kept
        pursuant to an order issued under § 1010.370 of this chapter shall be retained
        for the period of time specified in such order, not to exceed five years.
        All such records shall be filed or stored in such a way as to be accessible
        within a reasonable period of time, taking into consideration the nature of
        the record, and the amount of time expired since the record was made.


        [ 75 FR 65812 , Oct. 26, 2010, as amended at 81 FR 76864 , Nov. 4, 2016]

      - Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate under the combined
      44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive the acquisition

      - BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with missing underlying
      documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent CIP/AML
